root_cause.text: The netfilter xt_multiport v1 checkentry functions failed to validate the pflags/ports[] range encoding, so malformed rules could make ports_match_v1() consume a nonexistent or invalid next ports[] element and read past the last valid entry.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “ports_match_v1() treats any non-zero pflags entry as the start of a port range and unconditionally consumes the next ports[] element,” while “the checkentry path currently validates protocol, flags and count, but it does not validate the range encoding itself”; the patch adds multiport_valid_ranges() to reject cases where a range start is the last slot, followed by another range start, or has ports[i - 1] > ports[i].

intent_record.intent_summary: Add validation for xt_multiport_v1 port ranges to reject malformed or reversed range specifications.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function named multiport_valid_ranges(const struct xt_multiport_v1 *multiinfo) was added. It iterates over multiinfo->count, skips entries where pflags[i] is not set, and for flagged entries validates that there is a following element, that the following element is not also flagged, and that ports[i - 1] is not greater than ports[i], returning false on any invalid condition and true otherwise.
intent_record.how: This adds runtime validation logic for multiport range definitions so malformed range encodings can be detected and rejected instead of being treated as valid. It prevents cases where a range marker appears without an endpoint, where two consecutive range markers occur, or where a range start is greater than its end.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add range validation to multiport_mt_check() so invalid multiport specifications are rejected with -EINVAL.
intent_record.what: The function multiport_mt_check() was changed from returning the result of check(...) directly as 0 or -EINVAL to first explicitly rejecting failed check(...) results with an if statement, and then performing an additional validation by calling multiport_valid_ranges(multiinfo), returning 0 on success or -EINVAL on failure.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now enforces an extra validation step after the existing protocol/flag/count check. Configurations that previously passed check(...) but contain invalid multiport range data will now be rejected with -EINVAL, preventing invalid match parameters from being accepted.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add port range validation to IPv6 multiport match checking so invalid multiport rules are rejected with -EINVAL.
intent_record.what: The function multiport_mt6_check() was changed from returning the result of check(...) directly as 0 or -EINVAL to first explicitly testing check(...) and returning -EINVAL on failure, then performing an additional validation by calling multiport_valid_ranges(multiinfo) and returning 0 on success or -EINVAL on failure.
intent_record.how: At runtime, IPv6 multiport match validation now rejects configurations not only when the existing protocol/flag/count check fails, but also when the port range data in multiinfo is invalid. This prevents invalid multiport range specifications from being accepted.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly adds validation of xt_multiport_v1 port range encoding, which matches the root cause: missing checkentry validation of pflags/ports[] allowed malformed range entries and out-of-bounds access in ports_match_v1().

The root cause is missing validation of multiport v1 range encoding (pflags/ports[]), which can lead to out-of-bounds reads in ports_match_v1(). This group directly adds port range validation in the multiport checkentry paths, including IPv6, to reject malformed rules with -EINVAL.

candidates.rationale: This checkentry path only validated proto/invflags/flags/count and did not validate the v1 pflags/ports[] range encoding, allowing malformed rules to pass and later trigger out-of-bounds access in ports_match_v1().

The IPv6 checkentry path had the same omission: it accepted xt_multiport_v1 rules without validating pflags/ports[] ranges, so malformed inputs could later cause ports_match_v1() to read a nonexistent next ports[] element.

This is the sink where the unchecked malformed range encoding is consumed. Because prior checkentry code did not validate that pflags/ports[] formed valid ranges, this call could lead to ports_match_v1() reading past the last valid ports[] entry.

vuln_statements.explanation: This IPv4 checkentry return path invoked generic validation but omitted any validation of xt_multiport_v1 pflags/ports[] range encoding. As a result, malformed rules were accepted and later caused ports_match_v1() to consume an invalid or nonexistent next ports[] element.

This is the direct consumption point for the unchecked xt_multiport_v1 range encoding. If checkentry accepted malformed pflags/ports[] data, ports_match_v1() could read past the last valid ports[] entry while interpreting a range.

This IPv6 checkentry path had the same missing xt_multiport_v1 range validation as the IPv4 path. By returning after only generic checks, it allowed malformed pflags/ports[] encodings to pass through and later trigger invalid access in ports_match_v1().

    [NETFILTER]: x_tables: unify IPv4/IPv6 multiport match
    
    This unifies ipt_multiport and ip6t_multiport to xt_multiport.
    As a result, this addes support for inversion and port range match
    to IPv6 packets.
    
    Signed-off-by: Yasuyuki Kozakai <yasuyuki.kozakai@toshiba.co.jp>
    Signed-off-by: Patrick McHardy <kaber@trash.net>

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes both the vulnerable consumer logic in `ports_match_v1()` and the relevant validation paths `checkentry_v1()` / `checkentry6_v1()`. The root cause is present: `ports_match_v1()` treats `pflags[i]` as meaning a range and then unconditionally reads the next element with `e = minfo->ports[++i];`. If a malformed rule sets `pflags` on the last valid element, this increments `i` and consumes a nonexistent next `ports[]` entry. The corresponding checkentry functions do not validate the `pflags`/`ports[]` range encoding at all. `checkentry_v1()` only returns `check(ip->proto, ip->invflags, multiinfo->flags, multiinfo->count);` and `checkentry6_v1()` does the same. The helper `check()` only validates protocol, inversion flags, match flags, and `count <= XT_MULTI_PORTS`; it does not verify that every `pflags[i]` implying a range has a valid following `ports[i+1]`, nor that the encoding is otherwise well-formed. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is absent.
